You asked why I didn't re-draw my yellow box after price broke the LTF FL. I used to do this, but the more I practice the more I am seeing the importance of the lowest TF FL that forms after price engulfs an important area. The higher scale FL's are useful for positioning, but the real orders seem to exist in the hidden 'inner' FL's that form when price first engulfs an important zone.

This is important because the size of the FL determines when/where you draw the next engulf. That is why I prefer drawing the LTF FL first...then see what other FL's set up in the vicinity that could be used to form a FO to grab some added LQ. The LTF FL (the yellow box used in this example) is my starting point for seeing what LQ traps might set up in the area.
More practice & more interesting patterns to see unfolding around S/R areas.

USD-CAD

Without the blue box, the FL that bounced price (see black arrow) wouldn't have been obvious. This setup also included a convincing bottom demand zone. When price breaks those lows, the herd is rushing to get short.The breakout trading LQ is what fuels YOUR trade, as price spikes down and pushes higher to post a new high.

Lots of practice seeing these sneaky zones set up. You know you've got a good one when price sets up a fake level just above it.

In my opinion, this concept is the most valuable out of everything that is discussed on RTM. If I was a beginner, this is where I would be spending my time. Learn to see price in terms of order flow and liquidity.
